title: RZD • Internal Communication System
subtitle: From fragmented interactions to a controlled communication loop

facts.label: scope
value: UX / UI system under strict enterprise constraints

value.text: Russian Railways operated a legacy internal service used for employee-to-management communication, document-related requests, and internal approvals and escalations.
The system was functionally complete, but operationally inefficient.
It supported processes — but did not structure them.
The system failed not at the interface level, but at the process level.
Symptoms:

items: Lack of transparency in request handling

value.text: System-level failure:
The core issue was not usability — it was lack of system-level clarity.
Users did not need a "better interface". They needed a controlled communication loop.
Instead of redesigning screens, the focus shifted to designing a system:
The interface became a reflection of system logic — not the other way around.
User interaction was reframed as a closed loop:
This loop defines the core behavior of the system.

value.alt: Behavior loop diagram — closed communication cycle
value.caption: Closed-loop communication model: request → status → review → response → evaluation → optional escalation.

items: OR Escalate request → Forward to higher manager → Loop continues

value.caption: Operational flow: from request entry through category selection, submission, manager review, and resolution or escalation.

value.text: All requests follow a clearly defined lifecycle: Draft → Sent → Received → Answered → Closed. Escalation branches from Answered and loops back to Received.

value.alt: State machine — request lifecycle with escalation branch
value.caption: Explicit state system: every request has a predictable path. Escalation is part of the system, not a workaround.

value.text: The system is structured as a layered architecture: User Input → Routing Logic → State Machine → Notifications → Interfaces.
UI is the last layer — not the first. The interface reflects system logic, it does not define it.

value.caption: Layered architecture showing that UI is the output of system logic, not its starting point.

value.text: ### Eligibility before booking

value.alt: UI Before / After — Decision moved from user interpretation to system-structured scenarios
value.caption: Decision moved from user interpretation → to system-structured scenarios

value.text: Before the redesign, availability was presented as raw data. Users had to interpret room types, conditions, and constraints manually, without understanding whether a scenario was actually valid. This created a gap between selection and eligibility.

After the redesign, availability is structured as decision-ready scenarios. The system incorporates user context — including constraints and conditions — into the way options are presented. Users no longer construct scenarios themselves. They select from options that are already aligned with system rules.
### Outcome before submission

The system does not use submission as a validation step anymore. Instead, it constructs a complete scenario before the user commits. All key elements — guests, dates, room type, and pricing — are resolved in advance. Subsidies are applied, constraints are accounted for, and the final outcome is visible. Submission becomes a confirmation, not a test.
1. Explicit State System
All requests operate within a clearly defined lifecycle. Eliminates ambiguity. Improves predictability.
2. Linear Communication Flow
Replaced fragmented interactions with a structured sequence. Reduces cognitive load. Enforces process consistency.
3. Category-Based Routing
Requests are classified at entry point. Enables correct routing. Reduces handling time.
4. Built-in Escalation
Escalation becomes part of the system, not a workaround. Supports hierarchical structures. Maintains accountability.
5. Feedback Loop
Users can evaluate responses. Closes communication loop. Introduces quality control.
6. Minimalist Interface Strategy

Due to constraints: no decorative graphics, reliance on typography and structure, contrast used as primary visual tool. Aligns with enterprise expectations. Ensures clarity under high information load.
A structured communication system embedded in a mobile interface.
Not just an app redesign — but a workflow control layer for enterprise communication.
The system transitioned from interface-driven interaction to process-driven communication.

This project demonstrates system thinking over screen-level design, ability to operate under strict enterprise constraints, focus on behavior modeling and process clarity, and designing control layers instead of isolated interfaces.
